newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News- Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News- Oct 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor believes the circumstances of his team's loss to India in their one-off Test match will be so removed from the upcoming Test series against the West Indies in Australia, the loss will have no bearing on this summer's Tests. Page 25.

Australian soccer's goalkeeper Mark Bosnich, currently playing for British club Aston Villa, has been interviewed by police and may face criminal charges after Tottenham fans complained about him giving a Nazi-style salute during a game on Saturday. Page 5.

South Australian goal attack Jacqui Delaney, who was instrumental in guiding her team to victory in the Australian netball titles for the first time in 13 years, has been selected in the Australian squad for this year's inaugural Fisher and Paykel Cup against New Zealand. Page 29.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A survey conducted for the Sydney Morning Herald by AGB McNair has found that Australian Rules is clearly winning the war of the football codes in Australia, with 51 percent of Australians interested in the sport, compared to only 39 percent in 1992. The popularity of rugby league has dropped from 57 to 50 percent in the same period, with Union falling from 28 to 26 percent. Page 25.

Former New South Wales batsman Adam Gilchrist took Western Australia to victory over the Blues yesterday with a 61 not out at North Sydney Oval. New South Wales captain Greg Matthews shouldered the blame for the defeat in his first match as captain, saying he let down the team with his various bowling changes. Page 26.

New Zealand again celebrated a sporting triumph over Australia, this time defeating the Australian team 3-0 in the Dunhill Golf Cup at St Andrews in Scotland on Saturday. Australian captain Greg Norman, with Wayne Riley and Steve Elkington, were beaten by their less-favoured rivals Grant Waite, Greg Turner and Frank Nobilo. Page 29.
THE AGE

Melbourne Tigers basketball coach Lindsay Gaze says so little separates his team from the Canberra Cannons that their semi-final series could be decided by the more fortunate team. The series, which begins in Canberra tonight, will be dependant on small things, according to Gaze, and he believes his team will need to put in a good defensive effort to defeat the Cannons. Page 8.

In the national women's hockey league, the Queensland Scorchers defeated the Canberra Strikers 5-2 in Canberra yesterday, taking the lead during the first round of the three-part Stix series. Hockeyroo power hitter Jenny Morris led Queensland to convert our of 11 corner attempts. Page 12.

The Collingwood Warriors debuted in the Ericsson Cup soccer championship by defeating reigning champions the Melbourne Knights 3-0 in front of a crowd of at least 10,000. The Warriors, who won the pre-season National Cup competition, have not lost their first six games since Heidelberg United set up a joint venture with AFL club Collingwood. Page 13.
HERALD SUN

Gai Waterhouse will have to attempt to bend the quarantine rules of two countries to get her horse Juggler into their year's Japan Cup. Juggler was not among the original entries for the A$5 million Cup on November 24 and was not given the first set of innoculations, which were to be administered by October 8. Page 88.

Australian Rules clubs have until 2 p.m. Friday to delist senior players to make room for newcomers from the national draft on Friday week. Under AFL rules, each club must leave a minimum three places for draft picks, and most fringe players should know ther fate in the next 48 hours. Page 86.

Veteran cyclist Stephen Pate showed he was still a force in the sport, despite a crippling back injury, as he won the fourth stage of the VicHealth cycling tour yesterday. The former world sprint champion has been in pain since being involved in a crash on Friday, but said he owed his ability to continue riding to his masseur Gary Miritis. Page 81.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

A court ruling in the Industrial Court hearing next week could decide whether Australian Rugby League players are free to decide where they wish to play after their current club contracts expire. The court will hear whether five-year loyalty agreements signed with the ARL are valid. Page 27.

Australian rugby union coach Greg Smith says fitness will be a key element in the selection of the Wallabies side to play the first Test against Italy next week. Prop Dan Crowley and five-eighth Scott Bowen, as well as the omission of Tim Gavin, will see three changes to the team which played in the last Test against South Africa in August, and further changes could come about with Garrick Morgan, Tim Horan and Jason Little back from injury. Page 27.

Damien Oliver will return from Hong Kong this week to ride champion stayer Doriemus in racing's historic A$1 million Caulfield Cup on Saturday. Oliver is hoping to replicate last year's success in winning both the Caulfield and Melbourne cups. Page 32.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
